newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher, trade a steady buyer.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher, trade a steady buyer.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed firmer as trade buying lifted the market out of its recent lull, dealers said.
They attributed the buying frenzy to business done overnight following the life-of-contract lows hit in the front two contracts on Tuesday.
Fund buying and short covering accounted for some of the day's volume estimated at a brisk 30,000 lots. Tuesday's official volume was 29,028 lots.
Open interest in May rose 4,222 to 30,184 lots.
The most-active May contract closed 0.76 higher at 73.85 cents per pound, traded 74.15 to 73.30 cents. Spot-March ended up 0.58 to 72.23 cents.

One floor source said a major fund sold 500 lots on the open, which were quickly bought by the trade. Speculators began covering short positions as the trade remained a steady buyer amid a dearth of sell orders throughout the day, fueling prices to the day's highs, he said.
Dealers expect the March contract to test resistance at 73.00 cents Thursday.
Certificated stocks, meanwhile, rose to 153,983 bales as of Tuesday.
